title: MS-DOS 6.22
summary: The final standalone release of Microsoft Disk Operating System, featuring DriveSpace disk compression, ScanDisk, Defrag, and MemMaker utility.
facts: DriveSpace replaced DoubleSpace after legal patent disputes with Stac Electronics.
Included MemMaker to optimize conventional 640KB RAM allocation by loading drivers into Upper Memory Blocks (UMBs).
Essential command line OS for PC gaming throughout the early-to-mid 90s.

title: Norton Commander 4.0
summary: The legendary dual-pane file manager for DOS, setting the standard for orthodox file managers with keyboard shortcuts and archive navigation.
facts: Originally created by John Socha in 1986 and acquired by Symantec.
Used text-mode character graphics to display side-by-side directory trees.
Popularized function key commands (F5 Copy, F6 Move, F7 Mkdir, F8 Delete).

title: Microsoft QBasic & Gorillas.bas
summary: The structured BASIC interpreter included with MS-DOS 5.0 and 6.x, packaged with iconic example games like GORILLA.BAS and NIBBLES.BAS.
facts: Based on QuickBASIC 4.5 but lacked a standalone compiler.
GORILLA.BAS featured explosive banana trajectory artillery combat atop city skyscrapers.
Introduced millions of young programmers to software development.

title: DOS Memory Managers (HIMEM.SYS & EMM386.EXE)
summary: System drivers enabling DOS applications and games to access memory above the 640KB barrier (High Memory Area, Expanded Memory EMS, and Extended Memory XMS).
facts: CONFIG.SYS configuration tweaking was mandatory for PC gamers to free conventional RAM.
Competing third-party tools like QEMM-386 and 386MAX offered aggressive RAM optimization.
Broke through the 8086 1MB physical memory addressing limitation.

title: DJGPP 32-bit C/C++ Development Suite
summary: Full-featured port of the GNU C/C++ compiler toolchain for 32-bit protected mode DOS computers using CWSDPMI DOS extenders.
facts: Created by DJ Delorie allowing gcc and g++ to build 32-bit flat-memory DOS executables.
Used to develop major PC games like DOOM, Quake, and Duke Nukem 3D.
Eliminated 16-bit memory segment barrier for high-performance software.
